interpretation.actual_identity: Existing mgm:* identities are reused. Their freeform descriptions carry specific behavior, limits, and provenance. Applicable Type namespaces are referenced in type_ids, without membership OP joins.
evidence_limits: Accepted DNS replies establish bounded path evidence, not universal Internet reachability.
Current source forces debug peer acceptance; authentication surfaces are not proof of enforcement.
Indirect uplink routing is experimental and defaults off.
Configured profiles and historical reports are not proof of a successful current build or live deployment.
interpretation.op_direction: element_id provides the Encounter Function; object_id receives it and bears the purpose.

operation: OpenWrt and batman-adv supply interface lifecycle, kernel routing, mesh forwarding and topology observations. Valid mesh-L3 identity is required; IPGen supplies it optionally, while static addressing is another provider.

Embedded Sentry observes eligible direct uplinks and probes external DNS responders using candidate pools and adaptive deadlines. Its direct callback updates MGM before exterior sentry.link telemetry. MGM treats ONLINE and TESTING as connected and owns the route effects.

The store separates local authoritative state from receiver-local observations of peers. IPv6 link-local multicast exchanges sender-owned state and sender-scoped witnesses; it does not relay third-party state.

Peer state, originator loss/recovery and local connectivity meet at the event boundary. Direct-provider throughput ranking feeds metric policy; the route manager applies IPv4 forwarding decisions and the firewall reconciler permits the required traffic.
CLI, readiness observation, readable names, optional LEDs and LuCI expose controls and evidence. AutoAP preserves optional management access. Generic and Pi provisioning compose deployment choices.
Build tooling, source-only tests, guides and reports support maintenance. The archived Python prototype remains inside the repository but outside current runtime functionality.
